summary.oneLiner: Diversified multi-country garment exporter that absorbed a brutal FY26 US-tariff shock on India (50%+) by shifting volumes to Vietnam/Bangladesh/Indonesia, still delivered record FY26 revenue (INR5,025 cr, +11.5%) and PAT (+17%), and is now positioned to re-accelerate India as tariffs normalize and India-UK/India-EU FTAs pull EU/UK sourcing into India — targeting 10%+ EBITDA margin from FY27 and INR6,000 cr+ revenue by FY28.
summary.business: PGIL designs, develops and manufactures a diverse range of garments for global brands and retailers across the US, Europe, UK, Japan, Canada and Australia, operating 25 manufacturing units with a combined annual capacity of over 100 million pieces across India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia and Guatemala. Its integrated model spans Design and Development, Global Manufacturing, Sourcing and Supply Chain, and Marketing and Distribution, serving marquee clients such as PVH, Kohl's, Ralph Lauren, Primark, Old Navy, GAP, Chico's, Macy's and Target.

currentContext.strengths: Multi-country manufacturing footprint across India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia and Guatemala, enabling tariff optimisation, de-risked sourcing and agility across evolving trade dynamics|Long-standing relationships with marquee global brands including PVH, Kohl's, Chico's, Ralph Lauren, Primark, Old Navy, GAP, Macy's, Target, Muji, Poligono and Aritzia|Global design network of 100+ designers across 10 locations combining local insights with international trends, enabling faster product development cycles|Vertically integrated end-to-end supply chain model spanning design & development, manufacturing, sourcing and marketing/distribution|Sustainability and compliance credentials (13+ certifications, solar power across all 5 Indian plants, water-saving technologies) supporting access to compliance-demanding brand partners|Credit rating upgraded to ICRA A+ Stable (long-term) and ICRA A1+ (short-term), reflecting balance-sheet strength
currentContext.strategies: Sustain a diversified, multi-geography manufacturing ecosystem (India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia, Guatemala) rather than depend on the competitiveness of a single geography|Sustain double-digit growth momentum, targeting a CAGR of 12-14% in the near term, and keep growing capacity in line with business opportunity|Complete and effectively ramp up the ongoing Bangladesh capacity expansion|Progress newer facilities, particularly Guatemala and Bihar, towards greater operational maturity and scale|Continue evaluating both in-house and partnership manufacturing opportunities across India, Bangladesh, Vietnam and Indonesia|Deepen relationships with existing global fashion brand customers while diversifying the customer base and adding new marquee names|Consolidate ownership in overseas subsidiaries where strategically relevant (increased stake in Indonesia's PT Pinnacle Apparels)|Leverage India's improving trade-agreement access (India-UK FTA, prospective India-EU FTA, reversal of penal US duty) to drive renewed India growth from FY27|Build scalable manufacturing in emerging Tier II ecosystems in India via the Bihar expansion, leveraging workforce availability and competitive operating costs|Target breakeven for the Guatemala operation in FY27, leveraging reinstated zero-tariff US access|Invest in automation in Vietnam to improve productivity and manage the wage curve|The Company maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations that governs its dividend intent. Personal guarantees have been extended by promoter directors Dr. Deepak Kumar Seth and Mr. Pulkit Seth against certain Company borrowings. Related-party transactions, including with subsidiaries and with PDS Limited (an entity over which KMP exercise significant influence), are conducted on arm's-length terms, with outstanding balances generally unsecured and interest-free except for a specific interest-bearing loan.
currentContext.expansion: Group installed capacity rose to 100.8 million pieces p.a. as of 31 March 2026 from 93.1 million pieces p.a. as of 31 March 2025, with additions across all locations except Guatemala during the year. Bangladesh, the largest base by both capacity and workforce, operates 9 manufacturing units producing over 59.7 million pieces annually (pre-expansion) at approximately 85% utilisation; an ongoing in-house expansion is on track for completion by H1 FY 2026-27 and is expected to add 6-7 million pieces of annual capacity. A parallel sustainability laundry facility in Bangladesh (95% of the ~Rs 90+ crore investment committed as of FY26) is scheduled for completion by end-Q1 FY27. In India, 8 owned factories across Gurugram, Chennai, Bengaluru and Muzaffarpur (Bihar) run 25.9 million pieces of annual capacity; the new Bihar facility, part of a strategy to expand into lower-cost Tier-2/Tier-3 manufacturing regions, has installed 400 of a planned 900 machines and added 1.4 million pieces of capacity to the India business, with four of the eight owned factories currently EU-approved and approvals for the rest in progress. The Company is also evaluating multiple in-house and partnership-factory projects to grow its footprint in Vietnam and Indonesia, while Guatemala's operations remain in a stabilisation phase as a nearshore base for the US market. Capital was deployed across three areas during the year: capacity addition (new production lines in Bihar and the Bangladesh expansion), technology/automation (robotics, 3D design platforms and AI-enabled tools), and sustainable infrastructure (the Bangladesh laundry project). With ongoing expansion, the Company is targeting 125-130 million pieces of capacity by FY 2027-28.
currentContext.mdna: Reversal of the 25% penal duty on India-origin exports and the India-UK FTA (signed July 2025), together with the prospective India-EU FTA, are expected to materially enhance India's export competitiveness and drive renewed India growth from FY27 onwards|US market demand was more resilient than initially anticipated during the year, with customer buying budgets remaining relatively stable despite tariff-driven inflationary pressure|Tariff pass-through to end consumers has been measured and category-specific, with retailers selectively raising prices; moderate recalibration in buying volumes was observed in certain segments|Vietnam and Indonesia delivered healthy overseas volume growth and improved capacity utilisation during the year|Bangladesh, the largest and most established manufacturing base, ran at approximately 85% utilisation with a strengthening order pipeline|Demand across Europe, the UK, Japan and Australia remained stable, with the Company focused on expanding customer share in these markets|Guatemala's reinstated full zero-tariff access to the US strengthens the commercial attractiveness of the facility and reduced operating losses during the year|Global textile and apparel industry is projected to grow at a 5.5% CAGR (2026-2030), driven by rising consumption, e-commerce expansion, technological advancement and sustainability trends|Global shift towards a China+1 sourcing strategy and nearshoring/supply-chain diversification are expected to benefit India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia and Guatemala as manufacturing hubs|Temporary pricing concessions extended to certain US customers during the tariff burden are being unwound, with new orders being priced on normal (non-concessional) terms|Bangladesh's order pipeline strengthened during the year, alongside utilisation of approximately 85%|New customers were added during the year and the Company continues to grow with them, alongside efforts to add other marquee brand names in the industry

risks.note: Changes in tariffs, particularly in the U.S. market, may impact pricing competitiveness and margins, potentially necessitating pricing adjustments and affecting profitability.
High exposure to select markets, especially the U.S., increases vulnerability to demand fluctuations and policy changes.
Global disruptions, including trade conflicts and logistics constraints, may delay deliveries and increase costs.
Cautious purchasing by global retailers and inventory corrections may lead to order variability and volume pressure.
Currency fluctuations impact margins given the Company's export-oriented revenue model.
Expansion into new geographies and the ramp-up of facilities, such as Bihar and Guatemala, may impact efficiency and margins in the short term.
Dependence on a limited number of large customers may expose the Company to order concentration risk.

thesis (one-liner): Diversified multi-country garment exporter that absorbed a brutal FY26 US-tariff shock on India (50%+) by shifting volumes to Vietnam/Bangladesh/Indonesia, still delivered record FY26 revenue (INR5,025 cr, +11.5%) and PAT (+17%), and is now positioned to re-accelerate India as tariffs normalize and India-UK/India-EU FTAs pull EU/UK sourcing into India — targeting 10%+ EBITDA margin from FY27 and INR6,000 cr+ revenue by FY28.
scorecard (yoy):
**Consolidated:**
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR1,314 cr | INR5,025 cr | Q4 +6.9%, FY +11.5% | Highest-ever quarterly & annual; driven by overseas volume + value-add (Vietnam/Bangladesh/Indonesia) |
| Adj. EBITDA (ex-ESOP) | INR135 cr | INR468 cr | Q4 +13.7%, FY +14% | |
| Adj. EBITDA margin | 10.3% | 9.3% | Q4 highest-ever | **Ex-tariff + ex-Bihar/Guatemala loss: Q4 = 10.9%, FY = 10.3%** |
| Tariff impact | INR5 cr | INR36 cr | one-off | US reciprocal tariff borne / discounts to US clients |
| Bihar+Guatemala incremental loss | INR3 cr | ~INR13 cr | ramp-up | new-facility drag |
| PAT (reported) | INR81 cr | INR270 cr | Q4 +24.6%, FY +17% | |

**Standalone (India):**
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | FY26 | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR304 cr | INR1,081 cr | India down sharply in Q4 (tariff-driven shift out of India) |
| Adj. EBITDA margin | 7.9% | 6.2% (+60bps YoY) | **Ex-tariff: Q4 = 9.6%, FY = 8%** (vs Q4 FY25 = 10.2%) |
| Tariff cost | INR5 cr | INR19 cr | |
| PAT | INR14 cr | INR69 cr | vs INR55 cr FY25 |

**Order book/visibility:** No hard order-book number disclosed (build-to-ship, not long-term orders). Mgmt: India order book + capacity "perfectly matching"; good traction returning to India post-tariff + FTA interest.

**Balance sheet / net debt:** Net worth INR1,438 cr (vs INR1,146 cr). Cash & bank (ex-LC-earmarked) INR634 cr (vs INR513 cr) — effectively net-cash/very low net debt. Working capital 43 days. ROCE 28%. Credit rating upgraded to **A+ stable / A1+** (from BBB/A3+ in 2021).

**Forex/realization:** Realization ~INR635–640 per garment; target INR600+ sustained. Per-unit swings with knits/wovens mix and low-FOB customers (e.g. Primark).
guidance (critical — explicit):
- **Revenue:** 12–14% CAGR target (group level); INR6,000 cr by FY28 "achievable even with modest 9% growth" — but mgmt confident of exceeding INR6,000 cr if leaders "stay sensible."
- **Margin:** **10% EBITDA on FULL-YEAR basis from FY27** (first milestone), trajectory **10–12%** over coming years. India: double-digit EBITDA in Q4 FY27 specifically; high-single-digit for India full-year.
- **Capacity:** Installed capacity crossed **101 mn pieces** (ahead of earlier H1 FY27 target). Target **125–130 mn pieces by FY28**, shipping ~100 mn pieces. Bangladesh capex adds 6–7 mn pieces by H1 FY27; +20 mn via partnership facilities.
- **Customer/geography adds:** Continuous client addition; pushing more Japanese brands (Fast Retailing group; NOT UNIQLO due to Muji conflict); EU/UK customers (currently in Bangladesh/Cambodia) engaging to add India capacity.
- **Guatemala:** breakeven targeted in FY27.
order book & pipeline:
- No formal order-book figure (model = strategic visibility + wallet-share, not long-term orders).
- India order book improving post-tariff; EU/UK customer interest rising on FTA expectation.
- Higher Q1 FY27 shipments expected (inventory days up in Q4 = pre-positioned for Q1 shipments).
- Capacity 25–30 mn-piece add over 2 yrs not fully customer-locked — strategic discussions give partial visibility only.
segment (by country/customer):
- **India (standalone):** Q4 contribution fell from ~32% to ~23% of mix; revenue degrowth ~23% YoY — direct fallout of 50%+ US tariff (Aug-25 onward); existing orders shipped out by Dec/Jan, then volumes pulled to other countries. Margins held (9.6% ex-tariff) despite deleverage.
- **Bangladesh:** smooth post new-elected-govt; strong export momentum (Europe, US, UK, Canada). Capex (washing + stitching units) completing H1 2027, +6 mn pieces over FY27–28. Was the major turnover contributor for 3–4 yrs.
- **Vietnam:** strongest growth this year. Utilization 80%+ (vs 63%). Key US-market hub. Buying land for greenfield (~$2.5–3 mn) to convert partner-heavy volume in-house.
- **Indonesia:** utilization 47% (vs 39%), premium-client focus; to deliver top+bottom line from FY27. Acquiring +10% of PT Pinnacle Apparels (→99.92% stake) for $1.4 mn.
- **Guatemala:** in "Others" segment, near-shore US; still loss-making, reworked strategy, breakeven targeted FY27.
- **Bihar (India):** new facility, ramp-up loss.
- **Key customers:** Muji (Japanese, crossed ~$65 mn, in top 6, India+Bangladesh sourced, growing); Primark (low-FOB); marquee customer recently added after 2-yr pursuit. Top US customers — PGIL at #1/#2/#3 vendor positions.
growth / optionality:
- **FTA tailwind (key non-obvious lever):** India-UK + India-EU FTAs → EU/UK retailers historically concentrated in Bangladesh/Cambodia (LDC duty-free) now want India presence. PGIL already serves these customers in Bangladesh → natural pull into India.
- **Comprehensive market access:** India (post-FTA preferential to US/EU/UK/Japan/Australia); Bangladesh/Vietnam/Indonesia already duty-free → uniquely diversified vs single-country peers.
- **Vendor consolidation:** brands grow ~7–8%; PGIL targets 12–14% via wallet-share gain (multi-location + multi-category), not just market growth.
- **Japan expansion:** Muji deepening; pursuing more Fast Retailing brands.
- **US business return to India:** partially, where India raw-material is competitive.
margins & cost:
- FY26 group margin 9.3% reported → 10.3% normalized (ex INR36 cr tariff + INR13 cr Bihar/Guatemala loss).
- FY27 10% target is "largely operational EBITDA" — not dependent on tariff reversal.
- Margin levers: cost restructuring (drove India +60bps), Bangladesh laundry capex (margin-accretive, no top-line), improving customer/product mix, Guatemala/Bihar loss reduction.
- Raw-material (cotton/polyester/energy) inflation pass-through within 1–2 months; mostly fixed at order booking (fabric ordered simultaneously).
capex:
- **FY26:** INR250 cr committed, completing H1 FY27 (on plan). CWIP INR110 cr (mostly Bangladesh).
- **FY27:** INR200–250 cr planned across geographies (could be MORE; ballpark, under evaluation). ~INR40–50 cr more capitalization → ~INR150 cr capitalizing in H1 FY27 → incremental depreciation.
- Vietnam greenfield land ($2.5–3 mn) + Indonesia stake-up ($1.4 mn) Board-approved in Q1 FY27.
capital allocation:
- **Dividend:** 2nd interim INR8.50/sh; **total FY26 = INR14.50/sh (290% of FV)** — highest-ever payout = **25% of group PAT**.
- Continued capex into India/Bangladesh/Vietnam (refused to halt India capacity despite tariff — "temporary").
- Bolt-on M&A (Indonesia minority buyout).
- Balance sheet near net-cash; rating upgrades reflect disciplined leverage.
risks:
- **US demand/tariff:** despite easing, ~10% Sec 122 tariff in place till July; residual burden-sharing continues (FY27 tariff cost may be ~INR5–8 cr, not zero); IEEPA refund saga uncertain. H2 US inflation/slowdown flagged by experts.
- **Country concentration shifts:** India revenue volatility (whipsawed -23% in Q4); reliance on tariff/FTA policy outcomes.
- **FTA implementation date unknown** — EU/UK upside is timing-dependent.
- **Ramp-up drag:** Bihar + Guatemala losses; Guatemala breakeven not yet achieved.
- **Demand cyclicality / consumer sentiment** (US inflationary environment).
- Partner-factory dependence (control risk if ratio skews >85% outsourced).
mgmt tone: Confident and measured. Repeatedly frames FY26 tariff shock as "temporary," emphasizes diversification as the moat. Strong conviction on 10% FY27 margin floor and INR6,000 cr+ FY28. Candid about India Q4 degrowth and Guatemala/Bihar losses (not glossed). Cautiously optimistic on US consumer resilience ("not seen 2022-type drop"). Closing: "a lot of optimism… well positioned for continued profitable growth."
non-obvious points:
- India tariff burden was disproportionate: customers asked PGIL to absorb the 25% *penalty* portion specifically on India goods → India-specific discounts/margin hit, not uniform across geographies.
- The "Others" segment spike (INR214 cr) is NOT Guatemala — it's build-to-ship billing for Bangladesh/Vietnam/Indonesia routed via US/Dubai/Indonesia entities; analyst misread it as Guatemala.
- Inventory-days rise is bullish (pre-positioned Q1 FY27 shipments), not a demand-weakness signal.
- Vietnam growth outran Bangladesh this year — diversification working; mgmt explicitly says no single country is "the" driver, rotates year to year.
- Design team scaled from ~70–75 to ~100+ people; investing in 3D design + AI rendering as a sales/adoption lever.
- INR635–640/garment realization is a useful proxy; volume math (100 mn pieces × ~INR600 = INR6,000 cr) reconciles the FY28 target.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- **Beneficiary of:** US-India trade normalization / India-UK & India-EU FTA → PGIL (and Indian apparel exporters broadly: Gokaldas Exports, KPR Mill, Arvind) gain from EU/UK sourcing-diversification away from Bangladesh/Cambodia.
- **China+1 / Bangladesh-shift / near-shoring** → multi-country footprint exporters (PGIL, PDS) vs single-country peers.
- ⭐ Vendor consolidation favors scaled, multi-category, multi-geography vendors → PGIL.
- US-tariff overhang on Indian cotton garments → adverse for India-only exporters; PGIL hedged via Vietnam/Bangladesh/Indonesia.

- **FTA tailwind (key non-obvious lever):** India-UK + India-EU FTAs → EU/UK retailers historically concentrated in Bangladesh/Cambodia (LDC duty-free) now want India presence. PGIL already serves these customers in Bangladesh → natural pull into India.

- **Vendor consolidation:** brands grow ~7–8%; PGIL targets 12–14% via wallet-share gain (multi-location + multi-category), not just market growth.

- **US business return to India:** partially, where India raw-material is competitive.
margins & cost:
- FY26 group margin 9.3% reported → 10.3% normalized (ex INR36 cr tariff + INR13 cr Bihar/Guatemala loss).

capex:
- **FY26:** INR250 cr committed, completing H1 FY27 (on plan). CWIP INR110 cr (mostly Bangladesh).

- Vietnam greenfield land ($2.5–3 mn) + Indonesia stake-up ($1.4 mn) Board-approved in Q1 FY27.
capital allocation:
- **Dividend:** 2nd interim INR8.50/sh; **total FY26 = INR14.50/sh (290% of FV)** — highest-ever payout = **25% of group PAT**.
- Continued capex into India/Bangladesh/Vietnam (refused to halt India capacity despite tariff — "temporary").
- Bolt-on M&A (Indonesia minority buyout).
- Balance sheet near net-cash; rating upgrades reflect disciplined leverage.
risks:
- **US demand/tariff:** despite easing, ~10% Sec 122 tariff in place till July; residual burden-sharing continues (FY27 tariff cost may be ~INR5–8 cr, not zero); IEEPA refund saga uncertain. H2 US inflation/slowdown flagged by experts.
- **Country concentration shifts:** India revenue volatility (whipsawed -23% in Q4); reliance on tariff/FTA policy outcomes.
- **FTA implementation date unknown** — EU/UK upside is timing-dependent.
- **Ramp-up drag:** Bihar + Guatemala losses; Guatemala breakeven not yet achieved.
- **Demand cyclicality / consumer sentiment** (US inflationary environment).
- Partner-factory dependence (control risk if ratio skews >85% outsourced).
mgmt tone: Confident and measured. Repeatedly frames FY26 tariff shock as "temporary," emphasizes diversification as the moat. Strong conviction on 10% FY27 margin floor and INR6,000 cr+ FY28. Candid about India Q4 degrowth and Guatemala/Bihar losses (not glossed). Cautiously optimistic on US consumer resilience ("not seen 2022-type drop"). Closing: "a lot of optimism… well positioned for continued profitable growth."
non-obvious points:
- India tariff burden was disproportionate: customers asked PGIL to absorb the 25% *penalty* portion specifically on India goods → India-specific discounts/margin hit, not uniform across geographies.
- The "Others" segment spike (INR214 cr) is NOT Guatemala — it's build-to-ship billing for Bangladesh/Vietnam/Indonesia routed via US/Dubai/Indonesia entities; analyst misread it as Guatemala.
- Inventory-days rise is bullish (pre-positioned Q1 FY27 shipments), not a demand-weakness signal.

- Design team scaled from ~70–75 to ~100+ people; investing in 3D design + AI rendering as a sales/adoption lever.

challenges → beneficiaries:
- **Beneficiary of:** US-India trade normalization / India-UK & India-EU FTA → PGIL (and Indian apparel exporters broadly: Gokaldas Exports, KPR Mill, Arvind) gain from EU/UK sourcing-diversification away from Bangladesh/Cambodia.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

hero.oneLiner: Diversified multi-country garment exporter that absorbed a brutal FY26 US-tariff shock on India (50%+) by shifting volumes to Vietnam/Bangladesh/Indonesia, still delivered record FY26 revenue (INR5,025 cr, +11.5%) and PAT (+17%), and is now positioned to re-accelerate India as tariffs normalize and India-UK/India-EU FTAs pull EU/UK sourcing into India — targeting 10%+ EBITDA margin from FY27 and INR6,000 cr+ revenue by FY28.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: PGIL designs, develops and manufactures a diverse range of garments for global brands and retailers across the US, Europe, UK, Japan, Canada and Australia, operating 25 manufacturing units with a combined annual capacity of over 100 million pieces across India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia and Guatemala. Its integrated model spans Design and Development, Global Manufacturing, Sourcing and Supply Chain, and Marketing and Distribution, serving marquee clients such as PVH, Kohl's, Ralph Lauren, Primark, Old Navy, GAP, Chico's, Macy's and Target.

segment_detail.title: Segment (by country/customer)
segment_detail.body:
- **India (standalone):** Q4 contribution fell from ~32% to ~23% of mix; revenue degrowth ~23% YoY — direct fallout of 50%+ US tariff (Aug-25 onward); existing orders shipped out by Dec/Jan, then volumes pulled to other countries. Margins held (9.6% ex-tariff) despite deleverage.
- **Bangladesh:** smooth post new-elected-govt; strong export momentum (Europe, US, UK, Canada). Capex (washing + stitching units) completing H1 2027, +6 mn pieces over FY27–28. Was the major turnover contributor for 3–4 yrs.
- **Vietnam:** strongest growth this year. Utilization 80%+ (vs 63%). Key US-market hub. Buying land for greenfield (~$2.5–3 mn) to convert partner-heavy volume in-house.
- **Indonesia:** utilization 47% (vs 39%), premium-client focus; to deliver top+bottom line from FY27. Acquiring +10% of PT Pinnacle Apparels (→99.92% stake) for $1.4 mn.
- **Guatemala:** in "Others" segment, near-shore US; still loss-making, reworked strategy, breakeven targeted FY27.
- **Bihar (India):** new facility, ramp-up loss.
- **Key customers:** Muji (Japanese, crossed ~$65 mn, in top 6, India+Bangladesh sourced, growing); Primark (low-FOB); marquee customer recently added after 2-yr pursuit. Top US customers — PGIL at #1/#2/#3 vendor positions.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — explicit)
guidance.body:

- **Margin:** **10% EBITDA on FULL-YEAR basis from FY27** (first milestone), trajectory **10–12%** over coming years. India: double-digit EBITDA in Q4 FY27 specifically; high-single-digit for India full-year.
- **Capacity:** Installed capacity crossed **101 mn pieces** (ahead of earlier H1 FY27 target). Target **125–130 mn pieces by FY28**, shipping ~100 mn pieces. Bangladesh capex adds 6–7 mn pieces by H1 FY27; +20 mn via partnership facilities.
- **Customer/geography adds:** Continuous client addition; pushing more Japanese brands (Fast Retailing group; NOT UNIQLO due to Muji conflict); EU/UK customers (currently in Bangladesh/Cambodia) engaging to add India capacity.
- **Guatemala:** breakeven targeted in FY27.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Reversal of the 25% penal duty on India-origin exports and the India-UK FTA (signed July 2025), together with the prospective India-EU FTA, are expected to materially enhance India's export competitiveness and drive renewed India growth from FY27 onwards
- US market demand was more resilient than initially anticipated during the year, with customer buying budgets remaining relatively stable despite tariff-driven inflationary pressure
- Tariff pass-through to end consumers has been measured and category-specific, with retailers selectively raising prices; moderate recalibration in buying volumes was observed in certain segments
- Vietnam and Indonesia delivered healthy overseas volume growth and improved capacity utilisation during the year
- Bangladesh, the largest and most established manufacturing base, ran at approximately 85% utilisation with a strengthening order pipeline
- Demand across Europe, the UK, Japan and Australia remained stable, with the Company focused on expanding customer share in these markets
- Guatemala's reinstated full zero-tariff access to the US strengthens the commercial attractiveness of the facility and reduced operating losses during the year
- Global textile and apparel industry is projected to grow at a 5.5% CAGR (2026-2030), driven by rising consumption, e-commerce expansion, technological advancement and sustainability trends
- Global shift towards a China+1 sourcing strategy and nearshoring/supply-chain diversification are expected to benefit India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia and Guatemala as manufacturing hubs
- Temporary pricing concessions extended to certain US customers during the tariff burden are being unwound, with new orders being priced on normal (non-concessional) terms
- Bangladesh's order pipeline strengthened during the year, alongside utilisation of approximately 85%
- New customers were added during the year and the Company continues to grow with them, alongside efforts to add other marquee brand names in the industry

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Group installed capacity rose to 100.8 million pieces p.a. as of 31 March 2026 from 93.1 million pieces p.a. as of 31 March 2025, with additions across all locations except Guatemala during the year. Bangladesh, the largest base by both capacity and workforce, operates 9 manufacturing units producing over 59.7 million pieces annually (pre-expansion) at approximately 85% utilisation; an ongoing in-house expansion is on track for completion by H1 FY 2026-27 and is expected to add 6-7 million pieces of annual capacity. A parallel sustainability laundry facility in Bangladesh (95% of the ~Rs 90+ crore investment committed as of FY26) is scheduled for completion by end-Q1 FY27. In India, 8 owned factories across Gurugram, Chennai, Bengaluru and Muzaffarpur (Bihar) run 25.9 million pieces of annual capacity; the new Bihar facility, part of a strategy to expand into lower-cost Tier-2/Tier-3 manufacturing regions, has installed 400 of a planned 900 machines and added 1.4 million pieces of capacity to the India business, with four of the eight owned factories currently EU-approved and approvals for the rest in progress. The Company is also evaluating multiple in-house and partnership-factory projects to grow its footprint in Vietnam and Indonesia, while Guatemala's operations remain in a stabilisation phase as a nearshore base for the US market. Capital was deployed across three areas during the year: capacity addition (new production lines in Bihar and the Bangladesh expansion), technology/automation (robotics, 3D design platforms and AI-enabled tools), and sustainable infrastructure (the Bangladesh laundry project). With ongoing expansion, the Company is targeting 125-130 million pieces of capacity by FY 2027-28.
